status: Theory and CPU diagnosis only; no GPU or new fitted vector

claims.claim: Self-generated successful trajectories can supply learning data
claims.evidence: STaR 3.1 Eq1-2 relates correctness-filtered likelihood gradients to expected-reward policy gradient; its actual greedy sampling and repeated updates are approximations
claims.limit: Does not establish correctness of every reasoning step or learned-vector compression; Appendix A/G/J explicitly discuss bad reasoning and lucky correct short outputs

claims.claim: Preference learning has a KL-regularized reward interpretation
claims.evidence: DPO Section4 Eq3-7 and AppendixA.1 derive pi*=pi_ref*exp(r/beta)/Z
claims.limit: General policy class, support and preference-model assumptions; finite data and a 1536-dimensional restricted vector do not inherit universal optimality or accuracy guarantees

claims.claim: Same-policy pair collection is a design control, not a DPO theorem prerequisite
claims.evidence: DPO Section4 describes reuse of offline preference datasets and reference mismatch; Section6 dialogue samples from an unknown model
claims.limit: Our current source conflict is association, not causal proof. Same-policy samples may still contain reasoning-style and correctness noise

claims.claim: Subtracting gamma from marked logits is a local KL-regularized proxy-cost optimum
claims.evidence: Own derivation: argmin_q KL(q||p)+gamma*E_q[1_marked] gives q_i proportional to p_i exp(-gamma*1_marked)
claims.limit: Proxy cost is not real reflection redundancy; gamma=ln2 and lexicon expansion have empirical, not optimality, support. At T=1 marked/unmarked odds halve, token probability does not generally halve. If penalty precedes T=.7, odds multiplier is 2^(-1/.7), before top-p truncation.

claims.claim: Conflicting group gradients can admit common ascent
claims.evidence: Own convex projection derivation: min-norm convex-hull point g* obeys Gi dot g* >= ||g*||^2 for every objective Gi
claims.limit: Only finite fixed-history surrogate objectives at initialization. Nonzero common group ascent is not every-parent, finite-step, online, accuracy, or token guarantee.
